newsitem.title: UK: UK natural gas mostly steady, front end firmer.
newsitem.headline: UK natural gas mostly steady, front end firmer.

text.p: U.K. natural gas prices were mostly steady on Monday as the market consolidated after frantic trade on Friday.
But firmer prices for October gas revealed a tight prompt market, traders said.
"There are still some people with requirements for October, and there's not a lot of gas around. We're completely maxed out," said one trader for a North Sea producer.
The rest of this week was sold at 13.50 pence a therm (p/th) at the National Balancing Point (NBP), while day ahead gas was traded at 14 p/th at St.Fergus on an entry assisted basis.
The St Fergus trade was the equivalent of around 13.5 pence a therm on a non entry assisted basis, a trader said.
But prices changed little across the rest of the forward curve and trade was thin.
"It's not unusually quiet for a Monday," said one dealer. "A lot got done last week so today people were holding back and working out their strategy for the week."
First quarter 1997 gas traded at 16 pence a therm at the NBP, after a spate of trades at between 15.80 p/th and 16.45 p/th on Friday.
"We've seen it settle just below where last discussions were on Friday," one broker said.
On the flexibility market, National Transmission System (NTS) operator Transco said that it received six system sell bids for Friday, the gas day Oct.18.
Transco sold a total of 117,315,434 kilowatt hours (4 million therms) of gas at an average bid price of 0.3963 pence per kilowatt hour (11.6 pence per therm.

No flex gas was traded over the weekend, the Transco spokeswoman said. Deals done: 14.00 pence a therm (day ahead, St.Fergus, 500,000 th/d, entry assisted) 13.50 pence a therm (22-25 Oct, NBP, 100,000 th/d) 14.30 pence a therm (Dec, NBP, 25,000 th/d) 14.35 pence a therm (Dec, NBP, 25,000 th/d) 16.00 pence a therm (Q1, NBP, 100,000 th/d) 15.05 pence a therm (March, NBP, vol n.c)
